\def\JFAArticleMain{1}
\begin{abstract}
Arbitrary-order first unmatched moment relative-entropy asymptotics under
Gaussian smoothing are due to Chen and Niles-Weed
\cite{ChenNilesWeed2022SmoothedWasserstein}, while all-order
stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work
\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017,
IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}.  Neither result is claimed as
new.  For the heavy-tailed isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable kernels,
\(0<\alpha<2\), we identify the optimal complete-moment condition that
transfers the density expansion through relative entropy.
If two
laws on \(\RR^d\) match all tensor moments below the integer order \(r\ge1\),
have a nonzero order-\(r\) difference \(\Delta_r\), and have finite
\(p_{r,\alpha,d}\)th absolute moments, where
\[
 p_{r,\alpha,d}=\max\left\{r,
 \frac{2r(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+2r}\right\},
\]
then
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
The coefficient is an orthogonally invariant positive-definite quadratic
form on symmetric order-\(r\) tensors.  The endpoint moment is sufficient.
When \(d+\alpha>2r\), every exponent
\(\rho\in[r,p_{r,\alpha,d})\) fails uniformly even for pairs with finite
nonzero \(\Delta_r\); when \(d+\alpha\le2r\), the threshold equals \(r\), and
smaller exponents fail only to define \(\Delta_r\) throughout the moment
class.  Thus the contribution is the heavy-tailed critical exponent,
endpoint sufficiency, and uniform sharpness, not the Gaussian quadratic
mechanism itself.

At every order \(r\), finite \(r\)th moments alone also give a law-by-law
decomposition: the universal quadratic tensor term plus a nonnegative
relative \(\Phi\)-energy between two positive proxies that retain each law's
unexpanded tail beyond the smoothing scale and their common lower-order jet.
To the best of our knowledge, this explicit positive proxy decomposition,
with vanishing of its KL term as an exact necessary and sufficient condition
for attainment of the universal coefficient, is new; no uniqueness or
canonicity of the proxy is asserted.  The defect is nevertheless unchanged
up to \(o(s^{-2r})\) by comparable hard or smooth cutoff scales and by common
bounded order-\(r\) proxy gauges; a partial rigidity result identifies this
gauge as the remaining freedom inside the retained-tail/common-core ansatz.
For the Cauchy kernel, the Cayley
transform additionally yields the exact equivalence between finite variance
and bounded \(t^4\) relative entropy, an all-order finite Laurent rule for the
subsequent coefficients, and a fully justified nonlocal Bregman tail identity
for the moving matched quotient.
\end{abstract}

% sec_introduction.tex -- Introduction
\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

The Cayley transform
\[
\iota(x)=\frac{1+\ii x}{1-\ii x}
\]
identifies the one-point compactification of \(\RR\) with \(\TT\), and pulls
normalized Haar measure back to the Cauchy law
\[
\omega(\dd x)=\frac{1}{\pi(1+x^{2})}\dd x=P_1(x)\dd x .
\]
This is the endpoint-normalized form of the classical Cauchy/wrapped-Cauchy
M{\"o}bius correspondence in circular statistics
\cite{KentTyler1988WrappedCauchy,McCullagh1992CauchyModels,
McCullagh1996CauchyMobius,
KatoJones2010MobiusCircle,KatoMcCullagh2020SphereCauchyMobius}.
This normalization makes the fixed-law Poisson comparison
\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-main-functional}
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma})\bigr)
\end{equation}
the object whose large-\(t\) behaviour is studied in Cayley--Chebyshev
modes.  The input law \(\nu\) is fixed, \(\bar{\gamma}\) is its mean, and
\(t\to\infty\) is the Poisson scale.

The basic calculation is a quotient calculation.  Let
\[
X_c=\gamma-\bar{\gamma}
\]
be the centred translation variable.  With \(x=\bar{\gamma}+ty\), translation
by \(X_c\) is encoded by
\[
R_\varepsilon(y)=\frac{1+y^2}{1+(y-\varepsilon)^2},
\qquad \varepsilon=X_c/t .
\]
The Cayley angle \(y=\tan\theta\) turns the Taylor coefficients of
\(R_\varepsilon\) into finite trigonometric, equivalently Laurent, modes.
After the matched Cauchy profile has been divided out, the quotient expansion
is therefore reduced to finite mode algebra; the KL expansion is then the
ordinary Taylor expansion of \((1+u)\log(1+u)-u\) in
\(L^\infty\cap L^1(\omega)\).

\subsection*{Contribution}

The principal unconditional result is
Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp-leading-kl-variance-threshold}.  For every law with
finite mean and without a tail-class assumption, finite centred variance is
equivalent to bounded \(t^4D_{\rm KL}\); the limit is \(\mu_2^2/8\) in the
finite-variance case and \(+\infty\) otherwise.  The infinite-variance proof
pairs the quotient with the bounded second Cayley mode and therefore does not
use a formal Taylor expansion.

The other principal analytic result is the regularly varying boundary theorem,
Theorem~\ref{cor:main-body-conditional-missing-top-moment-tail}.  For \(N\ge3\),
a centred law with two-sided regularly varying tails of index \(p=2N-2\) and
divergent integrated slowly varying factor
\(\ell_L(t)=\int^tL(s)\dd s/s\) satisfies
\[
t^{2N}\left\{H(t)-\sum_{j=2}^{N-1}A_{2j}(\nu)t^{-2j}\right\}
\sim p(c_++c_-)\kappa_N\mu_2\ell_L(t),
\qquad
\kappa_N=(-1)^N(N-1)2^{-2N+2}.
\]
Equivalently, the residual normalized by the truncated boundary moment has
limit \(\kappa_N\mu_2\).  This is a class-conditional analytic statement,
without a density, symmetry, or monotonicity assumption; it is not an
unconditional higher-order converse.

The all-order coefficient algebra has a different logical status.  For every
\(m\ge3\), the reduced universal polynomial satisfies
\[
A_{2m}^{\rm form}
=\kappa_m\mathfrak m_2\mathfrak m_{2m-2}
+P_m(\mathfrak m_2,\ldots,\mathfrak m_{2m-3}),
\qquad \kappa_m=(-1)^m(m-1)2^{-2m+2}\ne0.
\]
At \(m=2\), one instead has \(A_4^{\rm form}=\mathfrak m_2^2/8\).
Thus \(\EE|X_c|^{2m-2}<\infty\) is sufficient to evaluate every monomial and
is the minimal absolute-moment assumption that guarantees such evaluation
uniformly over all centred laws.  Proposition~\ref{thm:sharp-moment-equivalence-hierarchy}
is only this algebraic polynomial-domain minimality statement.  In particular,
for \(m\ge3\) it is not an unconditional converse for the entropy remainder.

The second theorem is multidimensional and finite-moment.  For
\(L\ge d+1\), finite centred \(L\)-moment closes the large-translation
remainder in the matched radial Poisson quotient, gives an explicit
\(L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_d)\) jet, supplies the large-\(t\)
entropy-existence package, and hence gives the tensor KL expansion through
order \(L+2\).  The two-region expression is retained as the quantitative
remainder bound; in this range the precise statement is the equivalence
\(\mathcal R_{d,L}(t)=o(t^{-L})\) for the two-region functional defined in
\path{sec_entropy_core_main.tex}, Definition ``Two-region remainder
functional,'' and the finite
\(L\)-moment assumption.
The restriction \(L\ge d+1\) is sharp for this \(L^\infty\) quotient
topology, as shown by the spike construction below.  It is not claimed to be
necessary for the leading KL coefficient in a weaker \(L^2(\Omega_d)\) or
entropy topology.  Section~\ref{sec:verified-A2-results} treats those weaker
topologies separately: the sharp moment exponent for the \(L^2\) quotient is
\(\max\{2,(d+1)/2\}\); finite covariance is the exact leading-KL threshold
for \(d\le3\); and finite covariance fails to control the leading KL scale
for every \(d\ge4\).  For every isotropic strictly \(\alpha\)-stable
kernel, the optimal uniform sufficient exponent among finite
absolute-moment assumptions is
\[
 p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
 \frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\},
\]
with the endpoint on the sufficient side; see
Theorem~\ref{thm:high-dimensional-kl-moment-threshold}.  This optimization
over moment classes is not a law-by-law necessity statement when
\(d+\alpha>4\).  The Gaussian boundary of the first-unmatched mechanism is
prior work.  Chen and Niles-Weed
\cite[Theorem~2.5]{ChenNilesWeed2022SmoothedWasserstein} write
\[
 \rho_t(x)=(2\pi t)^{-d/2}\exp(-|x|^2/(2t))
\]
and prove, under
\(\EE e^{\delta|X-\EE X|^2}+\EE e^{\delta|Y-\EE Y|^2}<\infty\), that if
the two laws first differ at order \(r=n+1\), then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-chen-niles-weed-kl}
 \lim_{t\to\infty}t^r
 D_{\rm KL}(\mu*\rho_t\|\eta*\rho_t)
 =\frac12\sum_{|\gamma|=r}
   \frac{|m_\gamma(\mu)-m_\gamma(\eta)|^2}{\gamma!}.
\end{equation}
With the spatial scale \(s=\sqrt t\), this is an \(s^{-2r}\) law.  If
\(g=\rho_1\), Gaussian Hermite orthogonality gives
\[
 \frac12\int\left\{
  \frac{(-1)^r}{g}\sum_{|\gamma|=r}
  \frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}\partial^\gamma g
 \right\}^{\!2}g\,\dd y
 =\frac12\sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{|\Delta m_\gamma|^2}{\gamma!}.
\]
Thus the positive quadratic tensor coefficient at an arbitrary first
unmatched order is not claimed here as a new mechanism.

Our increment is the heavy-tailed extension.  For \(0<\alpha<2\), the
Gaussian/Hermite and exponential-tail argument is replaced by a critical
stable translate-quotient estimate.  This determines the weakest uniform
complete-moment hypothesis, proves its endpoint with a little-\(o\)
remainder, and gives analytic counterexamples below it in the non-Hilbert
regime.  The mechanism holds at every first unmatched tensor order
\(r\ge1\).  With
\[
 q_{r,\alpha,d}=\min\left\{2,1+\frac{2r}{d+\alpha}\right\},
 \qquad
 p_{r,\alpha,d}=\frac{2r}{q_{r,\alpha,d}},
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
\(s^{-2r}\) quadratic tensor coefficient for two arbitrary inputs matching
all lower moments, under the endpoint \(p_{r,\alpha,d}\)-moment, and proves
that no smaller absolute-moment exponent works uniformly over the complete
moment class: for \(d+\alpha>2r\) this is analytic uniform sharpness on
pairs with a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor, whereas for
\(d+\alpha\le2r\) the value \(p_{r,\alpha,d}=r\) is only coefficient-domain
minimality below order \(r\).

The exact law-by-law interface also holds at every order.  Under only finite
\(r\)th moments and matching below \(r\),
Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition} retains
the common lower-order Taylor jet and each law's unexpanded exterior
translate mixture in positive densities \(k_{r,s}^\nu,k_{r,s}^\eta\).  It
proves
\[
 D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
 +D_{\rm KL}(k_{r,s}^\nu\|k_{r,s}^\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
\input{sec_introduction_proxy_robustness}
Thus the universal coefficient is attained exactly when the nonnegative
tail-proxy entropy is \(o(s^{-2r})\).  At covariance order against the
point mass at the common mean this reduces, up to \(o(s^{-4})\), to the
one-sided raw-tail \(\Phi\)-energy in
Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}.  When
\(d+\alpha\le4\), finite covariance forces that energy to vanish at the
required scale; when \(d+\alpha>4\), it is a genuinely additional
law-by-law condition.  The infinite
critical-moment boundary is genuinely different: Theorem
\ref{thm:critical-vague-tail-nonidentifiability} constructs two laws with the
same smooth multivariate regularly varying tail data and the same covariance,
one attaining the covariance coefficient and the other having unbounded
scaled entropy along a subsequence.
Theorem~\ref{thm:covariance-proxy-defect-decomposition} gives an
asymptotically exact
finite-covariance characterization of this distinction.  If
\(k_{\Sigma,t}\) denotes the positive Poisson density obtained by adjoining
the normalized quadratic mode \(t^{-2}b_\Sigma\) to the matched reference,
then
\[
 t^4H_d(t)=\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)
 +t^4D_{\rm KL}(h_t\|k_{\Sigma,t})+o(1).
\]
Thus attainment of the covariance coefficient is equivalent to the
vanishing of the complete nonlinear proxy defect.  This statement requires
only finite covariance and does not impose a density or tail regularity on
the original law.
The leading multidimensional covariance formula is deliberately read through
this analytic route.  Finite covariance alone determines the bounded quadratic
mode \(b_\Sigma\) and the algebraic number \(\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)\), but it
does not by itself make \(\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)\) the coefficient of
\eqref{eq:intro-main-functional}.  It becomes the leading KL coefficient only
after a quotient/existence bridge is in force, for example the
\((\mathrm{MPJ}_{d,L})+(\mathrm{EX}_{d,L})\) package supplied here by
finite \(L\)-moment with \(L\ge d+1\), or the separate second-order quotient
criterion stated in Section~\ref{sec:entropy-asymptotics}.

The nearest prior work for the heavy-tailed density estimates is
Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} and the refined follow-up
\cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}.  For every
\(0<\alpha<2\) and weighted moment order \(K\ge0\), those works subtract
moment-weighted derivatives of the stable heat kernel and prove scaled
\(L^q\) and weighted \(L^1\) remainder decay for the resulting density
expansion, including inhomogeneous and nonlinear refinements.  They do not
control the matched density quotient in
\(L^{q_{\alpha,d}}(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\dd y)\) or transfer that critical
estimate through relative entropy; those are the steps that produce
\(p_{\alpha,d}\) here.  They also do not retain the unexpanded translate
mixture beyond the smoothing scale as the nonlinear entropy energy in
Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}.
In contrast, Chen--Niles-Weed give the direct Gaussian KL precedent
\eqref{eq:intro-chen-niles-weed-kl}; the present comparison with the
fractional-diffusion literature is only a comparison of the heavy-tailed
analytic inputs and does not erase that priority.

The novelty claim is correspondingly narrow.  Arbitrary-order Gaussian
first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work, and all-order
stable/fractional density expansions are prior work.  To the best of our

"""Independent certificate for the verified A2 additions.

The symbolic rows prove the rational identities used in the manuscript.  The
quadrature rows are deterministic stress tests, not substitutes for the
analytic proofs: they test the moment-matched KL constant, the two-node Gauss
specialization, and the logarithmic Pareto square boundary on nontrivial laws.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
import sys
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from dataclasses import dataclass
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Iterable, Sequence

import mpmath as mp
import numpy as np
import sympy as sp
from numpy.polynomial.legendre import leggauss
from scipy.special import ndtri
from scipy.stats import qmc


@dataclass
class Check:
    name: str
    passed: bool
    evidence: str


def symbolic_checks() -> list[Check]:
    x, t = sp.symbols("x t", real=True, positive=True)
    a = sp.I * x / (2 * t - sp.I * x)
    checks: list[Check] = []

    p_density, q_density = sp.symbols("p_density q_density", positive=True)
    phi_delta = p_density * sp.log(p_density) - p_density + 1
    proxy_bregman = (
        p_density * (sp.log(p_density) - sp.log(q_density))
        - p_density
        + q_density
    )
    proxy_cross_entropy = p_density * sp.log(q_density)
    chain_residual = sp.simplify(
        phi_delta
        - proxy_bregman
        - proxy_cross_entropy
        + (q_density - 1)
    )
    checks.append(
        Check(
            "covariance-proxy KL chain identity",
            chain_residual == 0,
            "pointwise residual after restoring the zero-mass proxy mode "
            f"is {chain_residual}",
        )
    )

    recurrence_residuals = []
    for k in range(1, 9):
        residual = sp.simplify(a ** (k + 1) + a**k + t * sp.diff(a**k, t) / k)
        recurrence_residuals.append(residual)
    checks.append(
        Check(
            "pointwise Cayley-mode differential recurrence",
            all(value == 0 for value in recurrence_residuals),
            f"residuals={recurrence_residuals}",
        )
    )

    real_part = sp.simplify(-sp.re(a))
    checks.append(
        Check(
            "first-mode real part",
            sp.simplify(real_part - x**2 / (4 * t**2 + x**2)) == 0,
            f"-Re(a_t)={real_part}",
        )
    )

    resolvent = sp.simplify((1 + a) / (2 * t) - 1 / (2 * t - sp.I * x))
    checks.append(
        Check(
            "first-mode Laplace resolvent identity",
            resolvent == 0,
            f"residual={resolvent}",
        )
    )

    q = sp.symbols("q", nonnegative=True)
    moment_residuals = []
    for n in range(1, 9):
        finite_sum = sum((-1) ** (j - 1) * q**j for j in range(1, n))
        residual = sp.factor(q / (1 + q) - finite_sum - (-1) ** (n - 1) * q**n / (1 + q))
        moment_residuals.append(residual)

        Check(
            "all-even-moment remainder identity",
            all(value == 0 for value in moment_residuals),
            f"orders=1..8, residuals={moment_residuals}",
        )

    for r in range(1, 11):
        claimed = sp.Rational(1, 4) ** r * sp.binomial(2 * r - 2, r - 1)
        parseval = (
            sp.Rational(1, 2)
            * 2
            * sp.Rational(1, 4) ** r
            * sum(sp.binomial(r - 1, j) ** 2 for j in range(r))
        )
        constants_ok = constants_ok and sp.simplify(claimed - parseval) == 0
        constant_rows.append(f"C_{r}={claimed}")
    checks.append(

            "moment-matched Parseval constants",
            constants_ok,
            ", ".join(constant_rows),

        )

# Submission Metadata

## Target Journal

**Journal of Functional Analysis**

## Probability Alternative

**Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare, Probabilites et Statistiques** is the
thematically natural probability alternative.

## Fit Rationale

The paper's central increment is an arbitrary-order, law-by-law relative
entropy decomposition for isotropic strictly stable smoothing.  Under only
finite moments of the first unmatched order, it separates the universal
quadratic tensor coefficient from the KL divergence of two explicit positive
tail-jet proxies and makes vanishing of that proxy divergence the exact
coefficient-attainment criterion.  The proof rests on critical weighted
translate estimates, \(L^1/L^\infty/L^q\) transfer, Bregman geometry, and a
two-background Hessian argument.  This analytic architecture and its
nonlocal-semigroup applications make the Journal of Functional Analysis a
defensible first target.

The priority boundary is narrow.  Chen and Niles-Weed's arbitrary-order
Gaussian first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work.  All-order
stable/fractional heat-kernel density expansions are also prior work,
including those of Ishige, Kawakami, and Michihisa.  To the best of the
authors' knowledge, the new result is the stable law-by-law nonnegative
proxy-KL decomposition under only finite \(r\)-th moments, with its exact
vanishing criterion.  The manuscript makes no uniqueness or canonicity claim
for the proxy.

Acceptance at JFA remains uncertain on presentation, breadth, and priority.
The uncertainty is not that the central increment is below the journal's
theorem-level standard.  The Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare,
Probabilites et Statistiques remains a natural alternative because the
results also address stable laws, moment thresholds, and entropy asymptotics
as probability questions.

\title[Cayley--Poisson Entropy Asymptotics]{Cayley--Poisson Entropy Asymptotics}
\author{Anonymous author}
\date{}

\keywords{Cayley transform, Poisson semigroup, Cauchy generator, relative entropy

\subjclass[2020]{47D07, 60E10, 94A17, 42A38}

\begin{document}
\begin{abstract}
For a fixed probability law~\(\nu\) on \(\RR\) with mean \(\bar{\gamma}\), the
Cayley transform reduces the large-scale matched Poisson entropy
\[
  D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma}))
\]
to finite Laurent constant-term algebra.  The one-dimensional coefficient
hierarchy says that if \(\nu\) has finite centred
\((2N-2)\)th absolute moment, then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma}))
=\sum_{m=2}^{N}A_{2m}(\nu)t^{-2m}+o(t^{-2N}),
\]
where the universal polynomials \(A_{2m}\) are obtained from the
Cayley--Chebyshev modes by one constant-term rule.  The same method identifies
the sharp leading threshold:
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}t^4
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma})\bigr)
=\mu_2^2/8
\]
when the centred variance is finite, and diverges to \(+\infty\) when the
variance is infinite.

In \(\RR^d\), finite \(L\)-moment with \(L\ge d+1\) gives a matched radial
Poisson quotient with an explicit two-region \(L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_d)\)
remainder and hence tensor KL coefficients through order \(L+2\); the
\(\mathcal R_{d,L}(t)=o(t^{-L})\) decay of the displayed two-region
functional is equivalent to that finite-moment hypothesis in this range.
Under finite centred second moment, the
moving Cauchy quotient satisfies the exact nonlocal Bregman tail identity
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma}))
=\int_t^\infty \mathcal I_\nu(s)\,\dd s,
\]
after compact-window domain bounds.  Appendices collect related-work
comparisons and auxiliary coefficient-calculus and tail-verification checks;
they are not additional hypotheses for the three main theorems.
\end{abstract}
\maketitle

finite moments into tensor KL coefficients; and the moving-reference Cauchy
calculation gives the nonlocal Bregman tail identity for the matched
quotient.  The appendices that follow provide comparison, normalization, and
coefficient-check details without changing those hypotheses or conclusions.

\subjclass[2020]{47D07, 60E10, 94A17, 42A38}

\begin{document}
\begin{abstract}
For a fixed probability law~\(\nu\) on \(\RR\) with mean \(\bar{\gamma}\), the
Cayley transform reduces the large-scale matched Poisson entropy
\[
  D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma}))
\]
to finite Laurent constant-term algebra.  The one-dimensional coefficient
hierarchy says that if \(\nu\) has finite centred
\((2N-2)\)th absolute moment, then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma}))
=\sum_{m=2}^{N}A_{2m}(\nu)t^{-2m}+o(t^{-2N}),
\]
where the universal polynomials \(A_{2m}\) are obtained from the
Cayley--Chebyshev modes by one constant-term rule.  The same method identifies
the sharp leading threshold:
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}t^4
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma})\bigr)
=\mu_2^2/8
\]
when the centred variance is finite, and diverges to \(+\infty\) when the
variance is infinite.

In \(\RR^d\), finite \(L\)-moment with \(L\ge d+1\) gives a matched radial
Poisson quotient with an explicit two-region \(L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_d)\)
remainder and hence tensor KL coefficients through order \(L+2\); the
\(\mathcal R_{d,L}(t)=o(t^{-L})\) decay of the displayed two-region
functional is equivalent to that finite-moment hypothesis in this range.
Under finite centred second moment, the
moving Cauchy quotient satisfies the exact nonlocal Bregman tail identity
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_t*\nu\,\|\,P_t(\cdot-\bar{\gamma}))
=\int_t^\infty \mathcal I_\nu(s)\,\dd s,
\]
after compact-window domain bounds.  Appendices collect related-work
comparisons and auxiliary coefficient-calculus and tail-verification checks;
they are not additional hypotheses for the three main theorems.
\end{abstract}

The main text has three independent outputs.  The one-dimensional Cayley
calculus gives the finite Laurent coefficient hierarchy and the sharp
variance threshold; the multidimensional radial quotient estimates transfer
finite moments into tensor KL coefficients; and the moving-reference Cauchy
calculation gives the nonlocal Bregman tail identity for the matched
quotient.  The appendices that follow provide comparison, normalization, and
coefficient-check details without changing those hypotheses or conclusions.

   1: \begin{unnumberedproposition}[Robustness of the positive tail-jet convention]
   2: Assume the hypotheses and notation of
   3: Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Call a
   4: pair \((\chi,H)\) an admissible tail-jet convention if there are constants
   5: \(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\), such that
   6: \[
   7:  0\le\chi_s\le1,\qquad
   8:  \chi_s(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
   9:  \chi_s(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b),
  10: \]
  11: where each \(\chi_s:\RR^d\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and if
  12: \[
  13:  \int H_s\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}=0,
  14:  \qquad
  15:  \sup_s\bigl(\|H_s\|_\infty+
  16:         \|H_s\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}\bigr)<\infty.
  17: \]
  18: The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws.  Define
  19: \begin{align*}
  20:  \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda
  21:   &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
  22:  V_{s,\chi}^\lambda(y)
  23:   &:=\int\chi_s(x/s)F_y^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),\\
  24:  A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
  25:   &:=1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
  26:        \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s.
  27: \end{align*}
  28: For all sufficiently large \(s\), these are positive probability densities
  29: relative to \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\), their relative entropy
  30: \[
  31:  \mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
  32:  :=\int A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}
  33:  \Phi\!\left(
  34:   \frac{A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
  35:        {A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}}
  36:  \right)\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
  37: \]
  38: is finite, and
  39: \[
  40:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
  41:  =\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
  42:   +\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
  43: \]
  44: Consequently, for any two admissible conventions \((\chi,H)\) and
  45: \((\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H)\),
  46: \[
  47:  \left|\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\chi,H}(\nu,\eta)
  48:        -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\widetilde\chi,\widetilde H}(\nu,\eta)\right|
  49:  =o(s^{-2r}).
  50: \]
  51: Thus the vanishing criterion and the Hessian constant
  52: \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\) are independent of the convention in
  53: this class.
  54: 
  55: The class contains the original hard cutoff, every hard cutoff
  56: \(\mathbf1_{\{|x|>c_s\,s\}}\) with
  57: \(0<\inf_sc_s\le\sup_sc_s<\infty\), and smooth radial cutoffs
  58: \(\theta(|x|/(c_s\,s))\), where \(\theta=0\) on \([0,1]\) and \(\theta=1\)
  59: on \([2,\infty)\).  It also permits arbitrary measurable, nonradial,
  60: \(s\)-dependent transitions in a fixed annulus and the infinite-dimensional
  61: family of common bounded zero-mass gauges \(H_s\).
  62: \end{unnumberedproposition}
  63: 
  64: \begin{proof}
  65: Write \(F_y=F_y^{(\alpha,d)}\), let \(\mathsf B_j(y,z)\) be as in the proof
  66: of Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, and put
  67: \(q_s^\lambda(y)=\int F_y(x/s)\lambda(\dd x)\).  Direct addition and
  68: subtraction of the Taylor terms gives the exact split
  69: \[
  70:  q_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}
  71:   +s^{-r}(B_r^\lambda-H_s)+R_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
  72: \]
  73: where
  74: \begin{align*}
  75:  R_{s,\chi}^\lambda
  76:  &=\int(1-\chi_s(x/s))
  77:    \left\{F_\cdot(x/s)-\sum_{j=0}^r
  78:                   \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\right\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
  79:  &\quad-\sum_{j=1}^r\int\chi_s(x/s)
  80:                   \mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
  81: \end{align*}
  82: On \(|z|\le b\), the stable-kernel estimates and translation continuity
  83: used in \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-local-remainder} give a bounded function
  84: \(\omega_b\), with \(\omega_b(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\), such that the
  85: sum of the \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})\) norms of the Taylor
  86: remainder is at most \(\omega_b(|z|)|z|^r\).  Since \(1-\chi_s(x/s)\)
  87: vanishes for \(|x|\ge bs\), multiplication by \(s^r\) leaves a quantity
  88: dominated by \(C_b|x|^r\) and converging pointwise to zero.  Dominated
  89: convergence handles the first line.  For \(1\le j\le r\), the support
  90: condition on \(\chi_s\) and \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-mode-bounds} give
  91: \[
  92:  \left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
  93:              \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_\infty
  94:  +\left\|\int\chi_s(x/s)\mathsf B_j(\cdot,x/s)
  95:              \lambda(\dd x)\right\|_1
  96:  \le C_{a,r}s^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x).
  97: \]
  98: It follows that
  99: \[
 100:  \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_\infty+
 101:  \|R_{s,\chi}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-r}).
 102: \]
 103: The same tail estimate yields
 104: \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
 105: 
 106: Positivity and normalization are structural.  Indeed,
 107: \(V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\ge0\),
 108: \(\int V_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 109: =\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\), and both \(C_{r-1,s}\) and \(H_s\) have zero
 110: mean.  Moreover,
 111: \[
 112:  \inf_yA_s^{\lambda;\chi,H}(y)
 113:  \ge1-\|C_{r-1,s}\|_\infty-
 114:        \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda-s^{-r}\|H_s\|_\infty\longrightarrow1.
 115: \]
 116: The entropy is finite by the same mixture argument as in
 117: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-normalized-proxy-entropy}.  More explicitly, if
 118: \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda>0\), convexity of relative entropy gives, for
 119: \(Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda=V_{s,\chi}^\lambda/\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\),
 120: \[
 121:  \int Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\log Q_{s,\chi}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 122:  \le\frac1{\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda}
 123:  \int\chi_s(x/s)\{C_{\alpha,d}+(d+\alpha)
 124:               \log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
 125: \]
 126: The finite first moment implied by the finite \(r\)th moment proves the last
 127: inequality.  Adding the uniformly bounded terms
 128: \(C_{r-1,s}-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s\) preserves finite positive
 129: entropy.  The case \(\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=0\) is immediate.
 130: 
 131: Apply the two-background KL perturbation lemma with
 132: \[
 133:  A_{1,s}=A_s^{\nu;\chi,H},\quad
 134:  A_{2,s}=A_s^{\eta;\chi,H},\quad
 135:  B_{1,s}=B_r^\nu-H_s,\quad B_{2,s}=B_r^\eta-H_s.
 136: \]
 137: The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1\), and their common jet and common
 138: gauge cancel, so
 139: \[
 140:  \|A_s^{\nu;\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\chi,H}\|_1
 141:  \le2(\tau_{s,\chi}^\nu+\tau_{s,\chi}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
 142: \]
 143: All remaining hypotheses have just been verified.  Finally,
 144: \((B_r^\nu-H_s)-(B_r^\eta-H_s)=B_{\Delta_r}\), so the lemma's Hessian is
 145: exactly \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  This proves the expansion.
 146: Subtracting the expansions for two conventions proves the asserted
 147: \(o(s^{-2r})\) difference and the two invariant conclusions.
 148: \end{proof}

 150: \begin{unnumberedproposition}[Partial rigidity within the retained-tail ansatz]
 151: Fix an admissible retention profile \(\chi\).  Consider positive normalized
 152: proxies of the form
 153: \[
 154:  \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda-
 155:                          \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda,
 156:  \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
 157: \]
 158: where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
 159: \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
 160: jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
 161: \(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
 162: \(S_s^\lambda\) such that
 163: \[
 164:  q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
 165:  \qquad
 166:  \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
 167: \]
 168: Then
 169: \[
 170:  H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
 171: \]
 172: is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
 173: \[
 174:  \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
 175:  +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
 176: \]
 177: In particular,
 178: \[
 179:  \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
 180:  +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
 181: \]
 182: Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
 183: common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
 184: law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
 185: one initially writes the normalized proxy as
 186: \(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar counterterm, then
 187: normalization forces \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda\) exactly.
 188: \end{unnumberedproposition}
 189: 
 190: \begin{proof}
 191: The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
 192: rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
 193: proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
 194: terms agree, subtraction gives
 195: \[
 196:  s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
 197:    =s^r(R_{s,\chi}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
 198: \]
 199: The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
 200: \(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
 201: and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
 202: \(H_s\), and
 203: \(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
 204: \end{proof}
 205: 
 206: \paragraph{Scope of the rigidity statement.}
 207: The result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
 208: order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
 209: ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
 210: it is a partial rigidity result and not a uniqueness or canonicity theorem
 211: for all positive proxy constructions.

At every order \(r\), finite \(r\)th moments alone also give a law-by-law
decomposition: the universal quadratic tensor term plus a nonnegative
relative \(\Phi\)-energy between two positive proxies that retain each law's
unexpanded tail beyond the smoothing scale and their common lower-order jet.
To the best of our knowledge, this explicit positive proxy decomposition,
with vanishing of its KL term as an exact necessary and sufficient condition
for attainment of the universal coefficient, is new; no uniqueness or
canonicity of the proxy is asserted.  The defect is nevertheless unchanged
up to \(o(s^{-2r})\) by comparable hard or smooth cutoff scales and by common
bounded order-\(r\) proxy gauges; a partial rigidity result identifies this
gauge as the remaining freedom inside the retained-tail/common-core ansatz.
For the Cauchy kernel, the Cayley
transform additionally yields the exact equivalence between finite variance
and bounded \(t^4\) relative entropy, an all-order finite Laurent rule for the
subsequent coefficients, and a fully justified nonlocal Bregman tail identity
for the moving matched quotient.
\end{abstract}

+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

 206: It remains to compare the two normalizations.  Put \(\epsilon=s^{-r}\),
 207: write \(A_s^\lambda=A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}\) and
 208: \(\tau_s^\lambda=\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\), and interpolate by
 209: \[
 210:  X_{s,\theta}^\lambda
 211:  :=\frac{A_s^\lambda+\theta\tau_s^\lambda}
 212:          {1+\theta\tau_s^\lambda},\qquad 0\le\theta\le1.
 213: \]
 214: Thus \(X_{s,0}^\lambda=A_s^\lambda\) and
 215: \(X_{s,1}^\lambda=\widetilde A_s^\lambda\).  We first record the entropy
 216: estimate that replaces an unavailable \(L^\infty\) bound on the retained
 217: potential.  The preceding mixture bound, the bounded negative part of
 218: \(q\log q\), and \(\log(1+u)\le C_{a,r}u^r\) for \(u\ge a\) give
 219: \begin{align*}
 220:  \int V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
 221:        \log^+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}
 222:  &\le C\tau_s^\lambda
 223:    +C\int\chi_s^\lambda(x/s)
 224:           \{1+\log(1+|x|/s)\}\lambda(\dd x)\\
 225:  &\le C\tau_s^\lambda
 226:    +Cs^{-r}\int_{|x|>as}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)
 227:  =o(\epsilon).
 228: \end{align*}
 229: For fixed \(0<c<C<\infty\), the elementary pointwise bound
 230: \[
 231:  h(b+u,b'+v)\le C_{c,C}
 232:  \{(b-b')^2+u+v+u\log^+u+v\log^+v\},
 233:  \quad h(x,y)=x\log(x/y)-x+y,
 234: \]
 235: holds for \(c\le b,b'\le C\) and \(u,v\ge0\).  To see this, use the
 236: quadratic Taylor bound for \(h\) when \(u+v\le1\); when \(u+v>1\), absorb
 237: the constant in \(u+v\) and use the defining formula for \(h\).
 238: The bounded cores of \(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\) and
 239: \(X_{s,\theta}^\eta\) differ by
 240: \(O(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(\epsilon)\), uniformly in \(\theta\), while
 241: their nonnegative retained parts obey the last display.  Consequently,
 242: uniformly for \(0\le\theta\le1\),
 243: \[
 244:  D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)=o(\epsilon),
 245:  \qquad
 246:  \|X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta\|_1=o(\epsilon).
 247: \]
 248: 
 249: Let \(K_s(\theta)=D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu
 250: \|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)\) and
 251: \(a_s^\lambda(\theta)=\tau_s^\lambda/(1+\theta\tau_s^\lambda)\).
 252: Since
 253: \(\partial_\theta X_{s,\theta}^\lambda
 254: =a_s^\lambda(\theta)(1-X_{s,\theta}^\lambda)\), differentiation gives
 255: \begin{align*}
 256:  K_s'(\theta)
 257:  &=a_s^\nu(\theta)\int(1-X_{s,\theta}^\nu)
 258:        \log\frac{X_{s,\theta}^\nu}{X_{s,\theta}^\eta}
 259:        \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\\
 260:  &\quad-a_s^\eta(\theta)\int
 261:        \frac{(X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)
 262:              (1-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)}{X_{s,\theta}^\eta}
 263:        \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}.
 264: \end{align*}
 265: The second integral is \(o(\epsilon)\), because all interpolants have a
 266: common positive lower bound and \(|1-y|/y\) is bounded there.  For the first
 267: integral, use
 268: \[
 269:  \int(1-x)\log(x/y)\dd\Omega
 270:  =\int\log(x/y)\dd\Omega-D_{\rm KL}(x\|y),
 271:  \qquad
 272:  \int|\log(x/y)|\dd\Omega\le c^{-1}\|x-y\|_1.
 273: \]
 274: It too is \(o(\epsilon)\).  Since
 275: \(a_s^\lambda(\theta)=o(\epsilon)\), uniformly in \(\theta\), we obtain
 276: \(\sup_{0\le\theta\le1}|K_s'(\theta)|=o(\epsilon^2)\).
 277: The preceding finite-entropy estimates justify the differentiation; one may
 278: equivalently truncate the retained potentials and pass to the limit using
 279: the displayed integrable bounds.  Integration from zero to one proves
 280: \[
 281:  \widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}
 282:  -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}=o(s^{-2r}).
 283: \]
 284: Combining this with the additive expansion proves all remaining assertions.
 285: \end{proof}
 286: 
 287: \begin{unnumberedproposition}[Asymptotic coefficient rigidity inside a prescribed ansatz]
 288: Fix an admissible pair \(\boldsymbol\chi=(\chi^\nu,\chi^\eta)\).  Consider
 289: positive normalized
 290: proxies of the form
 291: \[
 292:  \widehat A_s^\lambda=1+J_s+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda-
 293:                          \tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda,
 294:  \qquad \lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\},
 295: \]
 296: where \(J_s\) is common to the two laws and has zero
 297: \(\Omega_{\alpha,d}\)-mean.  Suppose the proxies are order-\(r\)
 298: jet-faithful in the following precise sense: there are zero-mean modes
 299: \(G_s^\lambda\), uniformly bounded in \(L^\infty\), and remainders
 300: \(S_s^\lambda\) such that
 301: \[
 302:  q_s^\lambda=\widehat A_s^\lambda+s^{-r}G_s^\lambda+S_s^\lambda,
 303:  \qquad
 304:  \|S_s^\lambda\|_\infty+\|S_s^\lambda\|_1=o(s^{-r}).
 305: \]
 306: Then
 307: \[
 308:  H_s:=s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})
 309: \]
 310: is a common zero-mean family bounded in both \(L^\infty\) and \(L^1\), and
 311: \[
 312:  \|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_\infty
 313:  +\|G_s^\lambda-(B_r^\lambda-H_s)\|_1=o(1).
 314: \]
 315: In particular,
 316: \[
 317:  \|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_\infty
 318:  +\|G_s^\nu-G_s^\eta-B_{\Delta_r}\|_1=o(1).
 319: \]
 320: Thus, within this ansatz, the lower-order common jet is forced modulo the
 321: common order-\(r\) gauge already allowed by the robustness result, and the
 322: law-difference mode, hence its Hessian, is forced asymptotically.  Also, if
 323: one initially writes the normalized proxy as
 324: \(1+J_s+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda+c_s^\lambda\) with a scalar
 325: counterterm, then normalization forces
 326: \(c_s^\lambda=-\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\) exactly.
 327: \end{unnumberedproposition}
 328: 
 329: \begin{proof}
 330: The last assertion follows by integrating the proposed proxy.  For the
 331: rigidity statement, compare the assumed split with the exact split in the
 332: proof of the robustness proposition with \(H=0\).  Since the retained-tail
 333: terms agree, subtraction gives
 334: \[
 335:  s^r(J_s-C_{r-1,s})+G_s^\lambda-B_r^\lambda
 336:    =s^r(R_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda-S_s^\lambda).
 337: \]
 338: The right side tends to zero in both stated norms.  Boundedness of
 339: \(B_r^\lambda\) and \(G_s^\lambda\) therefore proves the bounds on \(H_s\)
 340: and the claimed approximation.  Subtracting the two law identities cancels
 341: \(H_s\), and
 342: \(B_r^\nu-B_r^\eta=B_{\Delta_r}\), which proves the final display.
 343: \end{proof}
 344: 
 345: \paragraph{Scope of the coefficient-rigidity statement.}
 346: This is asymptotic coefficient rigidity inside the prescribed ansatz.  The
 347: result does not select a retention profile, remove the common
 348: order-\(r\) gauge, compare proxies outside the retained raw-tail/common-core
 349: ansatz, or assert that the proxy minimizes relative entropy.  In particular,
 350: it is not a uniqueness, canonicity, or entropy-minimality theorem for all
 351: positive proxy constructions.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}

+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile

+\[

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.
+

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\end{align*}
+For fixed \(0<c<C<\infty\), the elementary pointwise bound
+\[
+ h(b+u,b'+v)\le C_{c,C}
+ \{(b-b')^2+u+v+u\log^+u+v\log^+v\},
+ \quad h(x,y)=x\log(x/y)-x+y,
+\]
+holds for \(c\le b,b'\le C\) and \(u,v\ge0\).  To see this, use the
+quadratic Taylor bound for \(h\) when \(u+v\le1\); when \(u+v>1\), absorb
+the constant in \(u+v\) and use the defining formula for \(h\).
+The bounded cores of \(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\) and
+\(X_{s,\theta}^\eta\) differ by
+\(O(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(\epsilon)\), uniformly in \(\theta\), while
+their nonnegative retained parts obey the last display.  Consequently,
+uniformly for \(0\le\theta\le1\),
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)=o(\epsilon),
+ \qquad
+ \|X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta\|_1=o(\epsilon).
+\]
+
+Let \(K_s(\theta)=D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu
+\|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)\) and
+\(a_s^\lambda(\theta)=\tau_s^\lambda/(1+\theta\tau_s^\lambda)\).
+Since
+\(\partial_\theta X_{s,\theta}^\lambda
+=a_s^\lambda(\theta)(1-X_{s,\theta}^\lambda)\), differentiation gives
+\begin{align*}
+ K_s'(\theta)
+ &=a_s^\nu(\theta)\int(1-X_{s,\theta}^\nu)
+       \log\frac{X_{s,\theta}^\nu}{X_{s,\theta}^\eta}
+       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\\
+ &\quad-a_s^\eta(\theta)\int
+       \frac{(X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)
+             (1-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)}{X_{s,\theta}^\eta}
+       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}.
+\end{align*}
+The second integral is \(o(\epsilon)\), because all interpolants have a
+common positive lower bound and \(|1-y|/y\) is bounded there.  For the first
+integral, use
+\[
+ \int(1-x)\log(x/y)\dd\Omega
+ =\int\log(x/y)\dd\Omega-D_{\rm KL}(x\|y),
+ \qquad
+ \int|\log(x/y)|\dd\Omega\le c^{-1}\|x-y\|_1.
+\]
+It too is \(o(\epsilon)\).  Since
+\(a_s^\lambda(\theta)=o(\epsilon)\), uniformly in \(\theta\), we obtain
+\(\sup_{0\le\theta\le1}|K_s'(\theta)|=o(\epsilon^2)\).
+The preceding finite-entropy estimates justify the differentiation; one may
+equivalently truncate the retained potentials and pass to the limit using
+the displayed integrable bounds.  Integration from zero to one proves
+\[
+ \widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}
+ -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}=o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Combining this with the additive expansion proves all remaining assertions.
 \end{proof}

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and

+ \qquad

+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.

+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.
+

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+quadratic Taylor bound for \(h\) when \(u+v\le1\); when \(u+v>1\), absorb

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

# PDF Skill

## When to use
- Read or review PDF content where layout and visuals matter.
- Create PDFs programmatically with reliable formatting.
- Validate final rendering before delivery.

## Workflow
1. Prefer visual review: render PDF pages to PNGs and inspect them.
   - Use `pdftoppm` if available.
   - If unavailable, install Poppler or ask the user to review the output locally.
2. Use `reportlab` to generate PDFs when creating new documents.
3. Use `pdfplumber` (or `pypdf`) for text extraction and quick checks; do not rely on it for layout fidelity.
4. After each meaningful update, re-render pages and verify alignment, spacing, and legibility.

## Temp and output conventions
- Use `tmp/pdfs/` for intermediate files; delete when done.
- Write final artifacts under `output/pdf/` when working in this repo.
- Keep filenames stable and descriptive.

## Dependencies (install if missing)
Prefer `uv` for dependency management.

Python packages:
```
uv pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf
```
If `uv` is unavailable:
```
python3 -m pip install reportlab pdfplumber pypdf
```
System tools (for rendering):
```
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install poppler

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install -y poppler-utils
```

If installation isn't possible in this environment, tell the user which dependency is missing and how to install it locally.

## Environment
No required environment variables.

## Rendering command
```
pdftoppm -png $INPUT_PDF $OUTPUT_PREFIX
```

## Quality expectations
- Maintain polished visual design: consistent typography, spacing, margins, and section hierarchy.
- Avoid rendering issues: clipped text, overlapping elements, broken tables, black squares, or unreadable glyphs.
- Charts, tables, and images must be sharp, aligned, and clearly labeled.
- Use ASCII hyphens only. Avoid U+2011 (non-breaking hyphen) and other Unicode dashes.
- Citations and references must be human-readable; never leave tool tokens or placeholder strings.

## Final checks
- Do not deliver until the latest PNG inspection shows zero visual or formatting defects.
- Confirm headers/footers, page numbering, and section transitions look polished.
- Keep intermediate files organized or remove them after final approval.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+    def test_fixed_scale_robustness_scope_and_rigidity_are_explicit(self) -> None:
+        source = read_tex_source(ROOT / "sec_verified_A2_results.tex")
+        required = (
+            r"((\chi^\nu,\chi^\eta),H)",
+            "No relation between",
+            "Sharpness of the inner exclusion",
+            r"\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa",
+            r"(1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)",
+            r"\widetilde A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}",
+            r"\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}",
+            "normalization rules other than",
+            "Asymptotic coefficient rigidity inside a prescribed ansatz",
+            "not a uniqueness, canonicity, or entropy-minimality theorem",
+        )
+        for text in required:
+            self.assertIn(text, source)
+
+        abstract = (ROOT / "main.tex").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        intro = read_tex_source(ROOT / "sec_introduction.tex")
+        self.assertIn("either additive or multiplicative mass normalization", abstract)
+        self.assertIn("not every reasonable", intro)
+        self.assertNotIn("robust at its full resolution", intro)
+        self.assertNotIn("partial rigidity", abstract + intro + source)

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}\\
+ &\quad-a_s^\eta(\theta)\int
+       \frac{(X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)
+             (1-X_{s,\theta}^\eta)}{X_{s,\theta}^\eta}
+       \dd\Omega_{\alpha,d}.
+\end{align*}
+The second integral is \(o(\epsilon)\), because all interpolants have a
+common positive lower bound and \(|1-y|/y\) is bounded there.  For the first
+integral, use
+\[
+ \int(1-x)\log(x/y)\dd\Omega
+ =\int\log(x/y)\dd\Omega-D_{\rm KL}(x\|y),
+ \qquad
+ \int|\log(x/y)|\dd\Omega\le c^{-1}\|x-y\|_1.
+\]
+It too is \(o(\epsilon)\).  Since
+\(a_s^\lambda(\theta)=o(\epsilon)\), uniformly in \(\theta\), we obtain
+\(\sup_{0\le\theta\le1}|K_s'(\theta)|=o(\epsilon^2)\).
+The preceding finite-entropy estimates justify the differentiation; one may
+equivalently truncate the retained potentials and pass to the limit using
+the displayed integrable bounds.  Integration from zero to one proves
+\[
+ \widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}
+ -\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}=o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Combining this with the additive expansion proves all remaining assertions.
 \end{proof}

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and

+\[

+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,

+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.

+\[

+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+the corresponding additively normalized proxy with \(H=0\) satisfies
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+the corresponding additively normalized proxy with \(H=0\) satisfies
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+the corresponding additively normalized proxy with \(H=0\) satisfies
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}

+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta

+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.

+\[

+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}

+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below

+the corresponding additively normalized proxy with \(H=0\) satisfies
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}

+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile

+\[

**Mathematical Revisions**

The full revised statements and proofs are in [sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex:1).

The exact pair-of-profiles wording is:

> “Call \((\boldsymbol\chi,H)=((\chi^\nu,\chi^\eta),H)\) an admissible fixed-scale tail-jet convention if there are common constants \(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\) and \(\lambda\), such that
> \[
> 0\le\chi_s^\lambda\le1,\qquad
> \chi_s^\lambda(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
> \chi_s^\lambda(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b).
> \]
> … The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws. No relation between \(\chi_s^\nu\) and \(\chi_s^\eta\) is required beyond their common fixed inner and outer radii.”

All remainder and background estimates now use \(\chi^\lambda\) separately. In particular,
\[
\|A_s^{\nu;\boldsymbol\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H}\|_1
\le 2\bigl(\tau_{s,\chi^\nu}^{\nu}+\tau_{s,\chi^\eta}^{\eta}\bigr)
=o(s^{-r}).
\]

The origin-positive counterexample is placed immediately after the admissible-class definition. Its exact framing is:

> “The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically necessary at the resolution under study.”

For a smooth \(\chi=\kappa\in(0,1]\) near zero and compactly supported \(\nu,\eta\), the text proves, for the additive proxy with \(H=0\),
\[
\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,\qquad
V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,\qquad
A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1),
\]
and hence
\[
D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
=\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
The concluding exact wording is:

> “Thus adding the universal quadratic term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient \((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\). The retained raw tail has absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible class boundary is not a proof artifact.”

**Multiplicative Normalization**

The proposition now explicitly defines
\[
\widetilde A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
=\frac{1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s}
       {1+\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda}
\]
and proves
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}
-\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}=o(s^{-2r}).
\]

The proof interpolates by
\[
X_{s,\theta}^\lambda
=\frac{A_s^\lambda+\theta\tau_s^\lambda}
       {1+\theta\tau_s^\lambda}.
\]
The retained-mixture entropy estimate gives
\[
\int V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
       \log^+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\,d\Omega_{\alpha,d}
=o(s^{-r}),
\]
without assuming \(V\in L^\infty\). Uniformly in \(\theta\),
\[
D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}),
\qquad
\|X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta\|_1=o(s^{-r}),
\]
and differentiation of the interpolated KL gives
\(\sup_\theta|K_s'(\theta)|=o(s^{-2r})\). Thus (2a) closes at entropy level.

The statement still explicitly limits the result:

> “No assertion is made for proxy constructions outside this prescribed fixed-smoothing-scale tail/core class or for normalization rules other than the two displayed above.”

**Rigidity Wording**

The second proposition is now titled exactly:

> “Asymptotic coefficient rigidity inside a prescribed ansatz.”

Its scope paragraph says exactly:

> “This is asymptotic coefficient rigidity inside the prescribed ansatz. … In particular, it is not a uniqueness, canonicity, or entropy-minimality theorem for all positive proxy constructions.”

The abstract in [main.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/main.tex:123) and introduction fragments in [sec_introduction_proxy_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction_proxy_robustness.tex:1) and [sec_introduction_proxy_scope.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_introduction_proxy_scope.tex:1) now use “fixed-scale robustness” and “asymptotic coefficient rigidity,” include the order-\(r\) jet-faithfulness qualifier, and explicitly deny classification of all reasonable proxy conventions.

+\paragraph{Sharpness of the inner exclusion.}
+The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically
+necessary at the resolution under study.  Indeed, let a smooth profile
+\(\chi\) equal a constant \(\kappa\in(0,1]\) on a neighbourhood of zero and
+then rise to one, and let \(\nu,\eta\) be compactly supported, match below
+order \(r\), and satisfy \(\Delta_r\ne0\).  For all large \(s\),
+the corresponding additively normalized proxy with \(H=0\) satisfies
+\[
+ \tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,
+ \qquad V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1).
+\]
+Consequently,
+\[
+ A_s^\nu-A_s^\eta
+ =\kappa s^{-r}B_{\Delta_r}+o(s^{-r})
+ \quad\hbox{in }L^\infty\cap L^1(\Omega_{\alpha,d}),
+ \qquad \inf A_s^\eta\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+The quadratic KL expansion therefore gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
+ =\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+   +o(s^{-2r}),
+\]
+whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment} gives the
+actual smoothed entropy coefficient
+\(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  Thus adding the universal quadratic
+term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient
+\((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\).  The retained raw tail has
+absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible
+class boundary is not a proof artifact.

**Mathematical Revisions**

The full revised statements and proofs are in [sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_cayley_chebyshev_poisson_entropy_strip_rkhs_jfa/sec_tail_proxy_convention_robustness.tex:1).

The exact pair-of-profiles wording is:

> “Call \((\boldsymbol\chi,H)=((\chi^\nu,\chi^\eta),H)\) an admissible fixed-scale tail-jet convention if there are common constants \(0<a<b<\infty\), independent of \(s\) and \(\lambda\), such that
> \[
> 0\le\chi_s^\lambda\le1,\qquad
> \chi_s^\lambda(z)=0\quad(|z|\le a),\qquad
> \chi_s^\lambda(z)=1\quad(|z|\ge b).
> \]
> … The function \(H_s\) is common to the two laws. No relation between \(\chi_s^\nu\) and \(\chi_s^\eta\) is required beyond their common fixed inner and outer radii.”

All remainder and background estimates now use \(\chi^\lambda\) separately. In particular,
\[
\|A_s^{\nu;\boldsymbol\chi,H}-A_s^{\eta;\boldsymbol\chi,H}\|_1
\le 2\bigl(\tau_{s,\chi^\nu}^{\nu}+\tau_{s,\chi^\eta}^{\eta}\bigr)
=o(s^{-r}).
\]

The origin-positive counterexample is placed immediately after the admissible-class definition. Its exact framing is:

> “The condition that the profiles vanish near the origin is mathematically necessary at the resolution under study.”

For a smooth \(\chi=\kappa\in(0,1]\) near zero and compactly supported \(\nu,\eta\), the text proves, for the additive proxy with \(H=0\),
\[
\tau_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa,\qquad
V_{s,\chi}^\lambda=\kappa q_s^\lambda,\qquad
A_s^\lambda=1+C_{r-1,s}+\kappa(q_s^\lambda-1),
\]
and hence
\[
D_{\rm KL}(A_s^\nu\|A_s^\eta)
=\kappa^2\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}).
\]
The concluding exact wording is:

> “Thus adding the universal quadratic term to this proxy entropy would give the false coefficient \((1+\kappa^2)\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)\). The retained raw tail has absorbed a fixed fraction of the local order-\(r\) energy; the admissible class boundary is not a proof artifact.”

**Multiplicative Normalization**

The proposition now explicitly defines
\[
\widetilde A_s^{\lambda;\boldsymbol\chi,H}
=\frac{1+C_{r-1,s}+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda+s^{-r}H_s}
       {1+\tau_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda}
\]
and proves
\[
\widetilde{\mathcal E}_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}
-\mathcal E_{r,s}^{\boldsymbol\chi,H}=o(s^{-2r}).
\]

The proof interpolates by
\[
X_{s,\theta}^\lambda
=\frac{A_s^\lambda+\theta\tau_s^\lambda}
       {1+\theta\tau_s^\lambda}.
\]
The retained-mixture entropy estimate gives
\[
\int V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda
       \log^+V_{s,\chi^\lambda}^\lambda\,d\Omega_{\alpha,d}
=o(s^{-r}),
\]
without assuming \(V\in L^\infty\). Uniformly in \(\theta\),
\[
D_{\rm KL}(X_{s,\theta}^\nu\|X_{s,\theta}^\eta)=o(s^{-r}),
\qquad
\|X_{s,\theta}^\nu-X_{s,\theta}^\eta\|_1=o(s^{-r}),
\]
and differentiation of the interpolated KL gives
\(\sup_\theta|K_s'(\theta)|=o(s^{-2r})\). Thus (2a) closes at entropy level.

The statement still explicitly limits the result:

> “No assertion is made for proxy constructions outside this prescribed fixed-smoothing-scale tail/core class or for normalization rules other than the two displayed above.”
